title: Professional Judgement and Core Skills for Compliance Staff
summary: A ten-module programme building the judgement, questioning, advisory and writing skills that compliance, risk and financial crime staff need to be trusted by the business, the board and the regulator.
intro: This training programme equips compliance, risk and financial crime staff with the professional skills the role demands: forming and defending judgements, escalating well, advising the business, questioning effectively and writing clearly for the board and the regulator.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give compliance, risk and financial crime staff the practical judgement and professional skills that technical knowledge of the rules does not provide. Participants leave able to weigh evidence and reach defensible conclusions, advise and challenge the business, handle difficult conversations, escalate at the right time and write in a way that boards and supervisors trust.
sections.What It Covers: Professional judgement in the control functions, evidence and professional scepticism, cognitive bias, proportionality and prioritisation, advising the business, investigative questioning and fact-finding, difficult conversations, writing for the board and the regulator, escalation and breach decisions, and ethics and independence.
Intended Audience: Compliance, risk and financial crime analysts, officers and advisers in their first years in the role
Experienced control function staff moving into advisory, investigation or reporting roles who want to sharpen their judgement and writing
Business-side risk and control staff, such as first-line risk teams, who advise colleagues and escalate concerns
Learning Objectives: Explain why control function work depends on judgement and what makes a judgement defensible
Assess evidence with professional scepticism and recognise the biases that distort conclusions
Advise the business clearly and proportionately, and challenge it constructively
Apply investigative questioning and fact-finding techniques to breaches, complaints and internal reviews
Write clear, accurate and defensible papers, reports and correspondence for the board and the regulator
Decide when and how to escalate, and uphold ethical standards and independence under pressure
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, drafting exercises, role-play and peer feedback, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and control function structure.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of working in or alongside a compliance, risk or financial crime function is helpful. No legal qualification is required.
Core Reading: Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)
Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein, Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment (2021)
Rebecca Milne and Ray Bull, Investigative Interviewing: Psychology and Practice (1999)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)

modules.title: Professional Judgement in the Control Functions
modules.summary: Why compliance and risk work depends on judgement rather than rule-checking alone, where uncertainty comes from, and what it means to be personally accountable for a call.
objectives: Explain the role of judgement in risk-based compliance and risk work
Identify the sources of uncertainty in everyday control function decisions
Describe what a supervisor or reviewer will expect to see behind a judgement
syllabus: From checklist compliance to judgement-led advice and oversight
Ambiguous rules, incomplete facts and commercial pressure
The cost of over-cautious and under-cautious calls
Hindsight: how judgements are reviewed after the event

modules.title: Evidence, Professional Scepticism and Cognitive Bias
modules.summary: How to gather and weigh evidence, test the business's assertions rather than accept them, and recognise the biases that lead experienced professionals to the wrong conclusion.
objectives: Assess the reliability, relevance and sufficiency of evidence
Apply professional scepticism to management information and colleagues' assurances
Use simple techniques to counter individual and group bias
syllabus: Facts, evidence, opinion and assertion
Corroboration, triangulation and spotting inconsistencies
Confirmation bias, anchoring, optimism and groupthink
Pre-mortems, second opinions and recording the reasoning

modules.title: Proportionality and Prioritisation
modules.summary: How to match effort and response to the size of the risk, prioritise competing demands across a caseload, and avoid both gold-plating and under-reaction.
objectives: Apply proportionality to the nature, scale and impact of an issue
Prioritise work by risk, urgency and impact on customers and markets
Choose a response that fits the risk, from advice to escalation
syllabus: Proportionality in principle and in practice
Impact and probability: prioritising a caseload
Gold-plating, risk aversion and the cost to the business
Managing deadlines, workload and knowing when to ask for help

modules.title: Advising the Business
modules.summary: How to give advice on products, marketing, deals and change that is clear, practical and proportionate, so the business understands the risk and what it can do about it.
objectives: Establish the facts and the real question before giving advice
Give advice that sets out risks, options and conditions rather than a bare yes or no
Record advice so that it can be relied upon and evidenced later
syllabus: Understanding the business proposal and its commercial purpose
Structuring advice: issue, rule, risk, options and recommendation
Oral advice, emails and advice logs
Exercise: advising on a new product or financial promotion

modules.title: Investigative Questioning and Fact-Finding
modules.summary: How to plan and conduct fact-finding interviews and meetings for breaches, complaints, whistleblowing and internal reviews, obtaining reliable accounts and recording them accurately.
objectives: Plan a fact-finding interview with clear objectives and topics
Use open, probing and closed questions and active listening to obtain reliable accounts
Record interviews accurately and fairly for later reliance
syllabus: When an internal review needs interviews, and when to involve legal or HR
Questioning models: open, probing, closed and summarising
Handling evasive, defensive or senior interviewees
Role-play: a fact-finding interview after a suspected breach

modules.title: Managing Difficult Conversations
modules.summary: How to deliver unwelcome findings and advice, say no to senior colleagues, handle defensive or aggressive reactions and preserve the working relationship.
objectives: Explain why colleagues react defensively to control function findings
Apply a structure for delivering difficult messages clearly and fairly
Hold a position under pressure while keeping the relationship workable
syllabus: Types of difficult conversation in compliance and risk work
Preparing and structuring the conversation
Handling pushback, emotion and appeals to seniority
Role-play: telling a business head their launch cannot proceed as planned

modules.title: Writing for the Board and the Regulator
modules.summary: How to write papers, reports, file notes and regulatory correspondence that lead with the message, are precise and accurate, and stand up to scrutiny by directors, auditors and supervisors.
objectives: Structure documents so the key message and decision come first
Write in plain, precise and defensible language
Calibrate tone and accuracy for board papers and correspondence with the authority
syllabus: Top-down structure: conclusion first, then supporting evidence
Board and committee papers: what directors need to decide or note
Regulatory correspondence: accuracy, completeness and candour
Exercise: rewriting a weak paper and a weak letter to the regulator

modules.title: Escalation, Breaches and Notification Decisions
modules.summary: How to recognise when an issue must be escalated, write an escalation note that gets a decision, and reason through whether a breach is significant enough to notify the authority.
objectives: Identify escalation triggers and the right route in the firm
Assess the significance of a breach and the case for notification
Write an escalation note that sets out facts, risk and the decision required
syllabus: Escalation triggers, routes and timing
Assessing a breach: cause, impact, customers affected and recurrence
Notification judgements and the cost of late or partial disclosure
Exercise: escalating an emerging issue to senior management

modules.title: Ethics, Independence and Integrity
modules.summary: The ethical standards expected of control function staff, how independence is eroded in practice, and how to handle grey-area situations, conflicts and pressure to look the other way.
objectives: Recognise conflicts of interest and threats to independence in the control functions
Apply an ethical decision-making framework to grey-area situations
Know how to speak up and seek support when under pressure
syllabus: Independence, familiarity and capture by the business
Conflicts, gifts, hospitality and confidentiality in the second line
Speaking up and protection for those who raise concerns
Ethical dilemmas: case discussions from compliance practice

modules.title: Forming and Defending Judgements: Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a case study in which participants investigate an ambiguous issue, form and document a judgement, write it up for a committee and defend it under challenge.
objectives: Combine evidence, questioning, judgement and writing skills in a realistic scenario
Document reasoning so that it is defensible under later scrutiny
Defend a judgement before a mock committee and set personal development priorities
syllabus: Case briefing, analysis and a fact-finding interview
Recording the rationale: options considered and reasons for the decision
Drafting a short committee paper and escalation note
Workshop: presenting, defending and reflecting on the judgement
